body:
The analytic cliquet and performance engines use each reset interval's forward rate in theta. When spot and calendar-date forward rates and forward variances stay fixed as the curve reference dates advance, the time dependence is in the pre-reset discount factors. Using the interval rate can therefore disagree with the derivative of the engine's own value.

Use the dividend reference-date rate for cliquet and the risk-free reference-date rate for performance. The cliquet calculation retains its existing per-period conversion to the risk-free day counter. `forwardRate(d, d)` averages over the first 0.0001 curve years, so smooth-curve theta retains that approximation. Forward-option wrappers are unchanged.

For the call cases in `testThetaOnNonFlatCurves` with Actual/365 Fixed:

| Engine | Theta on `84fbf0a0e` | This PR | Central finite difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cliquet | 0.330287 | 0.0912821 | 0.0912821 |
| Performance | 0.00507849 | 0.00180367 | 0.00180367 |

The setup uses spot 100, volatility 25%, moneyness 105%, resets at 90/180/270 days and maturity at 360 days. Dividend forwards through days 30/120/240/400 are 1%/4%/1.5%/6%; risk-free forwards are 2%/5%/8%/3%. The finite difference shifts the evaluation and curve reference dates by ±1 day while retaining the calendar nodes.

The new test checks calls and puts for both engines, flat and non-flat curves, and Actual/365 Fixed or Actual/360 risk-free day counters, against finite differences at 1e-7 relative tolerance. The dividend day counter stays Actual/365 Fixed. Against `84fbf0a0e`, all eight non-flat assertions fail and all eight flat controls pass.

Implementation validation on Ubuntu 24.04 with g++ 13.3.0, Boost 1.83.0, Release and warnings as errors: all five `CliquetOptionTests` cases pass in C++17 and C++20. MSVC, Clang, AAD and the full suite were not run.

    ./build/test-suite/quantlib-test-suite --run_test=QuantLibTests/CliquetOptionTests --log_level=message

title: Fix theta of the cliquet and performance engines on non-flat curves
